name: Canonical Neural Radiance Field for X-ray Tomography
definition: A neural rendering technique that encodes the 3D density field of a static object (canonical volume) using a Neural Radiance Field, trained on rich projection data to serve as a prior for dynamic reconstruction.
summary: Canonical Neural Radiance Field for X-ray Tomography reconstructs 3D density fields by decoupling static volume representation from time-dependent deformation, outperforming methods that directly input time.
